title: review: landing: S2g contracts: per-role machine-validated worker output contracts and a bounded recovery ladder (deterministic
spec:
Land the reviewed change of T-1124 (branch task/T-1124, commits b0e043a, 631d90f; review verdict request_changes) onto the current goal/T-0991 head. In THIS worktree (fresh from goal/T-0991) cherry-pick the commits in order; resolve the conflicts (expected in orchestrator/promotion.py, orchestrator/spawn.py, tests/test_promotion.py, tests/test_spawn.py) by keeping BOTH sides' additions: the goal branch carries new subcommands, imports and tests from sibling tasks, the cherry-picked commits add this task's own; nothing is removed. Verify with the git log that the change sits on top of the goal head, then run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0. Do not change behaviour beyond conflict resolution; do not ask questions; report the resolved files and failures-only output.
Original task spec for reference (already implemented in the cherry-picked commits):
Create orchestrator/contracts.py. SCHEMAS per role: scout {findings: [{claim, location, confidence}], unresolved: [str], summary}, execute {summary, files_changed: [str], commits: [str], tests_run: [str], test_result: pass|fail|not_run, unresolved: [str]}, review and spec_review {verdict: approve|request_changes, findings: [{severity: high|medium|low, location, text}], required_changes: [str], risks: [str]}, challenge {claim, evidence: [str], agreement: agree|disagree|partial, confidence}, plus confidence and provenance on all (bus.post_result defaults). validate(role, result) -> {"ok": bool, "errors": [str], "repaired": dict|None}: deterministic repair first (key aliases such as files/changed_files, string-to-list coercions, verdict synonyms approve/approved/LGTM, confidence strings to float, drop unknown keys into extra); ok when the repaired result satisfies the schema. Recovery ladder in spawn.py at the point where extract_json runs on the worker output: 1 validate; 2 if not ok and [contracts].mode is active: one bounded schema-repair request resumed on the same session or thread (claude --resume session_id or codex resume) asking for only the JSON object for this role's schema, budget [contracts].repair_budget_usd (default 0.5) and one attempt; log a runs row role output_repair with tokens; 3 if still not ok, fall through to today's behaviour (review roles fail with no parseable verdict, others keep the raw result). [contracts].mode = "shadow" (dated comment): validate and record a decision_log row kind output_contract (add to KINDS) with role, ok, errors, repaired_keys, selected = accept|repair|rerun (shadow: what active would do), but never resume or change the stored result. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/13-output-contracts.md with the schemas and the shadow validation rate measured over the real task results on this repository (bus tasks with results, per role: ok, repairable, invalid).
Spec review T-1091 folded in: (1) Validation runs at every result-posting point, not only where extract_json runs: spawn.run_worker's non-execute branch, spawn's Claude-fallback execute branch, and executor.post_tool_result for Codex execute results (scope adds orchestrator/executor.py); each validates the dict it is about to post against the role schema, applies deterministic repair, records the decision_log row, and in active mode may use the bounded repair request where a session or thread exists. (2) The mode is a promotion feature: add contracts to promotion.FEATURES (scope adds orchestrator/promotion.py and tests/test_promotion.py) with criteria (30 shadow rows, repair success rate, no rise in failed results) and read it through promotion.mode("contracts"), never pool.cfg directly. (3) Interface contract, fixed here and mirrored into plan.md: contracts.SCHEMAS: dict role -> schema (required keys with types, optional keys, enums); contracts.validate(role, result) -> {ok: bool, errors: [str], repaired: dict | None}; contracts.repair(role, result) -> dict (deterministic, idempotent); contracts.recover(role, result, *, session=None, thread=None, budget_usd) -> {result, repaired_by: none|deterministic|model, tokens} used only in active mode.
Spec review T-1112 folded in (this supersedes the schema sketches above): SCHEMAS describe what the role prompts in .orchestrator/prompts/*.md actually ask workers to emit and what the code actually posts today; derive each schema from the prompt text and cite the prompt in the module docstring: review = {verdict: approve|request_changes, comments: [{path, line, issue, severity}]}; spec_review = {verdict: approve|request_changes, risks: [{path, issue, severity, line}], suggested_spec_changes}; challenge = {verdict: confirmed|refuted|uncertain, evidence: [str path:line], note}; scout = {findings: [{claim, evidence: [str], confidence, provenance}], open_questions, suggested_next, blocked}; execute (Codex path executor.post_tool_result and the Claude-fallback branch in spawn) = {summary, commit (string, may be empty), executed_by, provenance, usage, thread, rounds} with optional files_changed, tests_run, test_result; all with confidence and provenance defaults from bus.post_result. Deterministic repair covers verdict synonyms per role (approve/approved/LGTM; confirmed/refuted/uncertain synonyms), string-to-list coercions and confidence coercion only; no restructuring across shapes. decision_log rows of kind output_contract: candidates = ["accept", "repair", "rerun"], hard_constraints = ["schema:<role>"], deterministic = {ok, error_count, repaired_keys}, reason = the first error or "valid", selected = accept|repair|rerun, plus role and mode. promotion.collect gains a branch for "contracts" that reads output_contract rows (n, ok rate, repair rate) so promotion.report shows real evidence; the FEATURES criteria reference those numbers. The shadow measurement over the real bus results (main checkout, read-only) reports per role the ok, repairable and invalid shares under these prompt-derived schemas.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_output_contract_active_repair_resume_once_within_budget (patched resume returns valid JSON; runs row output_repair written)
tests/test_contracts.py::test_schemas_match_prompt_shapes (a fixture result in each prompt's documented shape validates ok for every role)
the worktree log between goal/T-0991 and HEAD contains the cherry-picked change and HEAD descends from the goal head

result.summary: Reviewed the scoped diff (b1910bd..3b46731) implementing orchestrator/contracts.py plus its wiring into spawn.py, executor.py, promotion.py, and decision_log.py, against the T-1112-superseded spec and acceptance list. SCHEMAS match the prompt-derived shapes in the docs table; repair() is idempotent and shape-preserving (verified via test_deterministic_repair_aliases_and_coercions and by tracing _coerce/alias logic); validate()/_errors() never leak result values, only schema paths and generic messages. process() correctly gates shadow (never resumes, never changes the stored payload, decision_log only) vs active (recover() invoked only when not preserve), and preserve=True (used for already-posted review/spec_review verdicts) skips recovery while still logging - matches 'audit an authoritative result without recovery'. recover()'s adapter contract (result/tokens/usd, budget and validity checked before accepting a model repair) matches test_recovery_is_bounded_and_preserves_invalid_original. spawn.py's resume_output wires --resume/--tools ''/--max-budget-usd correctly per test_output_contract_active_repair_resume_once_within_budget, and log_run is muted during the resume subcall to avoid double logging while output_repair rows are recorded separately. promotion.py's contracts feature (criteria, evaluate, collect) matches test_contracts_feature_registered and test_contracts_collect_reads_output_contract_rows exactly, including the path-traversal guard (Path(tid).name != tid) before reading task files by id. Traced the review/spec_review branch's widened existing_result lookup (now triggered whenever review_role, not just parse_failed) against T-1169's own fix-round history ('posted verdicts now take precedence') and confirmed via b1910bd diff that the asymmetric bus.post_result (only for role=='review', not spec_review) predates this change and is unaffected by it - not a regression introduced here. No new third-party dependencies; all new test methods are unittest.TestCase methods in files that import _harness first. Contract validation never places secret-shaped or raw result content into decision_log rows. No acceptance-relevant defect found; approving.
